newsitem.title: FRANCE: French air freight still hit by trucking dispute.
newsitem.headline: French air freight still hit by trucking dispute.

text.p: Industrial action by lorry drivers in several regions of France continues to disrupt airlines trucking services for airfreight, airport and airlines officials said.
The drivers began their action over wages, retirement age and working hours on November 18 by blocking major roads with an estimated 10,000 trucks.
Union representatives and road haulage bosses were meeting Thursday afternoon to discuss the dispute. South-West France was one of the regions hardest-hit, with the Bordeaux area particular affected.
"No trucks have left or arrived at Bordeaux airport for the past three days," an airport authority cargo official told Reuters.
However, some freight had unloaded from trucks and transferred to Air France Europe's passenger services to Paris.
As a result "to my knowledge, there is no backlog of freight to speak of at the airport." the airport official said.
A Lufthansa truck from Frankfurt heading to Bilbau via Bordeaux has been trapped in traffic since Monday (November 18), an airline official said on Thursday.
"For export traffic, we are continuing to get shipments up to Paris/CDG via a road/rail ransport platform located close to Bordeaux airport," he added
A similar situation to Bordeaux can be found at Toulouse airport where airlines have also used road/rail transport and scheduled passnger services to ship trucked airfreight.
British Airways said one of its trucks had arrived at CDG from Toulouse on Thursday six hours later than scheduled.

France Handling, the handling agents for around 30 airlines in France, said until Thursday its trucking services had not been badly affected by the lorry drivers action but it had since received reports of a "worsening situation" without having precise information at hand at present.
An Air France Cargo official in Marseille said truck journeys between Marseille and Paris/CDG were taking 24 hours instead of the normal 12 to 14 hours.
At Lyon the dispute appeared to be having less of an impact on trucked airfreight.

"Last (Wednesday) night, several trucks left Lyon for Paris and managed to reach arrive on time to meet ex-CDG flight connections and we are hoping the five truck departures scheduled for this (Thursday) evening will operate as smoothly," a cargo official for the French airline said. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
